DEPUTY CHAIRMAN in the Chair.Construction of road over Najafgarh drain*141.SHRI BHAGA T SINGH KOSHY ARI : Will the Minister of URBANDEVELOPMENT be pleased to refer to answers to Starred Questions 305, 289,Unstarred Questions 858, 2597, 3814 and 1060 given in the Rajya Sabha on the 6thDecember, 2007, 23rd July, 2009, 6th September, 2007, 26th November, 2009, 29thApril, 2010 and 18th November, 2010 respectively and state:(a)whether the Delhi Development Authority (DDA) would align and revisitthe requirement of road linkage in view of the survey ordered by Delhi Government toconstruct the required road over Najafgarh drain;(b)whether DDA would reconsider the proposal to cover Najafgarh drain, toavoid unnecessary uprooting of existing dwelling units, besides providing anenvironmental friendly way to utilise Najafgarh drain;(c)if not, the reasons for DDA not acting in synergy with Delhi Government;and(d)the steps being taken to prevent wastage of tax payers money due torepetitive work by multiple agencies?

DDA will act in synergy with this proposal of GNCTD toensure that the Urban Extension Roads get linked with the road on the Najafgarh drainfor improved city level traffic movements.Investigation into Pune bomb blasts†*142.SHRI MOHAN SINGH : Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS bepleased to state:(a)whether Government is aware that serial bomb blasts took place in Pune,Maharashtra on 1 August, 2012;(b)if so, whether its investigation has been completed; and(c)the elements suspected to be involved in these blasts and the steps beingtaken by Government to halt their activities?THE MINISTER OF STA TE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS (SHRIJITENDRA SINGH ) : (a) and (b)Yes, Sir. A series of five (5) Bomb Explosions tookplace at different places on the Junglee Maharaj Road in Pune City of Maharashtra on1st August, 2012 between 7.30 p.m. to 8.15 p.m. One unexploded bomb was alsorecovered which was later diffused by Police. The investigating agency viz. A TSMaharashtra is investigating the case.(c)No Terrorist Group has taken the responsibility yet for the above bombblasts. The monitoring of security arrangements in the country is an ongoing processand there exists a very close and effective coordination amongst intelligence agenciesat the Centre and State level. Intelligence inputs about possible designs and threats areshared with the State Governments concerned on a regular basis.The Government is committed to combating terrorism, extremism and separatismin all its forms and manifestation. While Law & Order and Police are State subjects,fighting terrorism is a shared responsibility because of its internal security implications.Government of India has continuously supplemented State Police capacities through† Original notice of the question was received in Hindi.

4Written Answers to[RAJYA SABHA] Starred Questionsthe Modernisation of State Police Forces Scheme under which, inter-alia, modernweaponary, fleet augmentation, upgradation of State Intelligence Units and traininginfrastructure are permissible heads of expenditure. At the National level, in order todeal with the menace of extremism and terrorism the Government has taken variousmeasures which, inter-alia, include augmenting the strength of Central Armed PoliceForces; establishment of NSG hubs at Chennai, Kolkata, Hyderabad and Mumbai;empowerment of DG , NSG to requisition aircraft for movement of NSG personnel inthe event of any emergency; strengthening and re-organizing of Multi-Agency Centreto enable it to function on 24×7 basis for real time collation and sharing of intelligencewith other intelligence and security agencies; tighter immigration control; effectiveborder management through round the clock surveillance & patrolling on the borders;establishment of observation posts, border fencing, flood lighting, deployment ofmodern and hi-tech surveillance equipment; upgradation of Intelligence setup; andcoastal security. The Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 has been amendedand notified in 2008 to strengthen the punitive measures to combat terrorism. TheNational Investigation Agency has been constituted under the National InvestigationAgency Act, 2008 to investigate and prosecute offences under the Acts specified in theSchedule. As a part of steps to counter terrorists threats, the National Intelligence Grid(NA TGRID) has been created.The Prevention of Money Laundering Act has been amended in 2009 to inter-alia, include certain offences under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, aspredicate offence.Further, the Government continues to raise the issues of Cross-Border Terrorismin all its aspects including its financing at various multilateral and bilateral fora.Deplorable conditions of archives and libraries*143.SHRI SHY AMAL CHAKRABORTY : Will the Minister of CULTUREbe pleased to state:(a)whether it is a fact that most of the country’s archives and libraries are ina state of ruin;(b)if so, what are the reasons behind this deplorable condition;(c)whether Government is contemplating any plan of action in this regard;and

Written Answers to[22 AUGUST, 2012]Starred Questions5(d)if so, the details thereof ?THE MINISTER OF CULTURE (KUMARI SELJA) : (a) and (b)The NationalArchives of India, New Delhi and libraries administered by the Ministry of Culturenamely National Library, Kolkata; Khuda Bakhsh Oriental Public Library, Patna;Rampur Raza Library, Rampur; Delhi Public Library, Delhi; Central Secretariat Library,New Delhi; Central Reference Library, Kolkata and Nehru Memorial Museum andLibrary, New Delhi are in good condition and providing excellent service to theresearchers, scholars and general public.State Governments also administer and support State libraries and archives. Theirmodernization, proper upkeep and maintenance is primarily the responsibility of therespective State Governments. Libraries and archives are also being run by privatesector/NGOs.(c) and (d)The Ministry of Culture, as the nodal Ministry for the preservationand conservation of cultural heritage including public records, has taken severalmeasures for improvement in the archives and libraries sector.Since 1986, National Archives of India (NAI) is providing financial assistance toState/Union Territory archival repositories for preservation, microfilming anddigitization of their records. NAI is also rendering technical assistance to various statearchives by way of organizing workshops on conservation of documents andmanuscripts. School of Archival Studies, NAI imparts training on various aspects ofRecords Management, Archives Administration, Preservation, Conservation andReprography etc. of short and long term duration to all stake holders including StateArchives, Ministries and Departments of Government of IndiaIn the libraries under the Ministry of Culture, a number of measures formodernization, renovation and preservation have been undertaken. The projects, inter-alia, include:1.Access to online full text journals in the National Library;2.Online public access catalogue for library users;3.Digitization of old and rare books including manuscripts;4.Conservation and preservation of rare books and manuscripts using moderntechniques etc.

Written Answers to[22 AUGUST, 2012]Starred Questions13All Party Delegation for permanent solution to problem of J and K†*150.SHRI NARENDRA KUMAR KASHYAP : Will the Minister of HOMEAFFAIRS be pleased to state:(a)whether any agreement has been arrived at by the All Party Delegation forthe redressal of the terrorism affected State of Jammu and Kashmir;(b)if not, the reasons therefor;(c)whether any negotiating committee had been setup for finding a permanentsolution of the problem of Jammu and Kashmir;(d)if so, the permanent solution devised in the report of the committee;(e)whether any permanent All Party Delegation will be set up for finding thepermanent solution of the problem of Jammu and Kashmir in future; and(f)if so, by when it will be set up?THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS (SHRIJITENDRA SINGH) : (a) and (b)Based on the visit of All Party Delegation sent toJammu and Kashmir, the Government has implemented an eight point plan to bringpeace to the State.(c) and (d)As a part of eight point plan, Government of India appointed threeInterlocutors on 13th October, 2010 to hold a sustained dialogue with all sections ofthe people in Jammu and Kashmir. The Interlocutors submitted their Report on 12thOctober, 2011. The Report has been uploaded on the website of this Ministry on 24thMay, 2012 for the benefit of the public at large. The copies of the Report have alsobeen placed in the Parliament Library for the benefit of the Hon’ble Members ofParliament.(e) and (f)Presently, there is no need felt for a permanent delegation and thereis considerable improvement in the law and order situation in J and K subsequent tothe implementation of Eight Point Plan of the Government of India and initiativestaken by the State Government.† Original notice of the question was received in Hindi.

Written Answers to[22 AUGUST, 2012]Starred Questions33(c)whether Districts Planning Committees set up under Article 243ZD arebeing brought into the processes of planning for the allocation of these funds;(d)the steps to ensure conformity with the provisions of the Panchayat(Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 (PESA) in deployment of IAP funds ; and(e)the Ministry’s assessment of the impact of IAP in capping, reversing andeliminating LWE?THE MINISTER OF STA TE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS (SHRIJITENDRA SINGH) :Statement(a) and (b)The Planning Commission is implementing the Integrated ActionPlan (IAP) for 82 Selected Tribal and Backward Districts, inter alia, including 71 LeftWing Extremism (LWE) affected districts for accelerated development of these districts.Initially, the implementation of the IAP was started in 60 Selected Tribal and BackwardDistricts with a block grant of Rs. 25 crore and Rs. 30 crore per district during 2010-11and 2011-12 respectively for which the funds were placed at the disposal of theCommittee headed by the District Collector and consisting of the Superintendent ofPolice of the district and the District Forest Officer. The coverage of the Scheme waslater extended to 82 districts based on the requests received from the State Governments.It has been decided to continue the implementation of the IAP in its present form in thefinancial year 2012-13 with a block grant Rs. 30 crore per district.(c) and (d)The performance of the Scheme is reviewed regularly. Reviewshave shown that the Scheme in its current format is performing extremely well. TheState Governments are also highly appreciative of the Scheme and want more districtscovered under its ambit.(e)The IAP has been under implementation since November 2010. Left WingExtremism is a complex problem which needs to be addressed at different levels. Itneeds intervention through a combination of security, development, governance andpolitical measures. The IAP is a scheme primarily to address the governance deficit inLWE affected areas and enhance the credibility of the district administration in theeyes of the local communities. This is necessary since the district administration is thelast tier in the country’s governance structure and the government’s credibility isreflected in the performance of the district administration. Under this Scheme, a totalnumber of 80,633 projects relating to public infrastructure and services have been

Written Answers to[22 AUGUST, 2012]Starred Questions35(b)if so, whether it has been found that many foreigners who visit India, visitvarious parts of the country without informing the police or concerned intelligenceagencies;(c)if so, whether a large number of foreigners, who have visited India havenot returned to their country, are declared as ‘missing’; and(d)if so, to what extent the strategy of Government to keep track of everyvisiting foreigner will check increasing illegal stay?THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS (SHRIMULLAPPALLY RAMACHANDRAN) : (a)Modernization and up-gradation ofImmigration services in the country is a Mission Mode Project being implemented bythe Ministry of Home Affairs under the National e-Governance Plan. The project istitled “Immigration, Visa and Foreigners, Registration & Tracking (IVFRT)”. ThisProject aims to develop a secure service delivery framework to enhance security andfacilitation by integrating the visa issuance process, Immigration functions and theForeigners’ Registration Process. The Project seeks to provide unified access to theImmigration and Law enforcement authorities about the visa application data,immigration data, registration data and other relevant information about stay and travelof the foreigners in India, for effective tracking of the foreigners. The total estimatedcost of the project is Rs. 1011 crore and the Project is to be implemented in a plannedand phased manner by September, 2014. With the implementation of this project, allthe Indian Missions across the globe, all Immigration Check Posts, Foreigners RegionalRegistration Offices and Foreigners Registration Offices in the country would be linkedwith the Central Foreigners Bureau.(b)The Registration of Foreigners Act, 1939 and the Registration of ForeignersRules, 1992 provide that certain categories of foreigners whose intended stay in Indiais more than 180 days or mandated under their visa authorization are required to getregistered with the Registration Officer i.e. concerned FRRO or FRO having jurisdictionover the place where the foreigner intends to stay, within 14 days of his/her arrival.Pakistani Nationals are required to get registered within 24 hours of arrival unlessspecifically exempted from the registration requirement. Therefore, all foreigners arenot required to inform the Police or intelligence agencies about their movement withinIndia.

As on 31.12.2011, 71035foreigners were overstaying in the Country.(d)The integrated database of the Unique Case files of the foreigners willhelp the Law enforcement authorities in identifying a traveller and keeping generalwatch over movement of the foreigners within India, generating alerts about overstayalsand taking appropriate legal action.Social security to unorganized workers*156.SHRI NAND KUMAR SAI : Will the Minister of LABOUR ANDEMPLOYMENT be pleased to state:(a)whether Government proposes to provide social security to unorganizedworkers, including landless agricultural labourers, in the country;(b)if so, the details in this regard;(c)the details of the initiatives taken by Government for such unorganisedworkers, including landless agricultural labourers, so far;(d)the number of landless agricultural labourers in various States as on date;and(e)the details of the expenditure likely to be incurred by Government forextending social security to such section of the society?THE MINISTER OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT (SHRI MALLIKARJUNKHARGE) : (a) to (c)With a view to providing social security to unorganised workers,including landless agricultural labourers, the Government enacted the “UnorganisedWorkers’ Social Security Act, 2008”. Written Answers to[22 AUGUST, 2012]Unstarred Questions117Citizenship to Hindus migrated from Pakistan1141.SHRI BHARA TSINH PRABHA TSINH PARMAR :SHRI PARSHOTTAM KHODABHAI RUPALA :Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state:(a)whether action has been taken by Ministry on the representation to empowerDistrict Collectors to grant Indian citizenship to Hindus migrated from Pakistan;(b)how many applications have been received by Government from refugeeHindu family migrated from Pakistan within last three years for shelter in India;(c)how many such applications are granted and how many applications areunder process during last three years; and(d)whether the Ministry has taken opinion of Ministry of External Affairsand State Governments in this regard?THE MINISTER OF STA TE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS (SHRIMULLAPPALLY RAMACHANDRAN) : (a) to (c)The grant of Indian citizenship isa multi-level and multi-agency activity. As per rules 11 and 12 of the CitizenshipRules, 2009, an application for grant of Indian citizenship is to be submitted by theapplicant to the Collector/DM/DC within whose jurisdiction the applicant is ordinarilya resident. The Collector/DM/DC after satisfying himself regarding eligibility of theapplicant to become a citizen of India, forwards the application to the State Government/UT administration concerned. The State Government/UT administration in turn forwardsthe application along with its recommendation to the Ministry of Home Affairs.Thereafter, the application is processed further as per the provisions of the CitizenshipAct, 1955 and the rules made there under. Since initial application is submitted to theCollector/DM concerned and a number of agencies are involved in the processing ofapplications for grant of citizenship, no case/religion based centralized data of suchapplications is maintained. All cases received in the Ministry of Home Affairs areprocessed as expeditiously as possible. 1290 applications of Pakistani nationals werereceived from various State Governments/UTs for grant of Indian citizenship byregistration and naturalization during last three years i.e. 2009 - 2011. Indian citizenshipwas granted to 764 Pakistan nationals during this period.(d)The MEA and State Governments concerned are consulted from time totime.

Written Answers to[22 AUGUST, 2012]Unstarred Questions163Cloudburst in Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand1168.SHRI MOHAN SINGH : Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleasedto state:(a)the number of people went missing and the number of those who lost theirlives due to cloudburst at Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand and the quantum of lossof life and property in both the States; and(b)the quantum of central assistance given to both these States by Governmentof India in order to deal with natural calamity?THE MINISTER OF STA TE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS (SHRIMULLAPPALLY RAMACHANDRAN) : (a)As per information received from theGovernment of Uttarakhand, 28 persons have lost their lives, 06 persons missing, 11persons have been reported injured, 80 cattle heads lost, and 71 houses (58 residential+ 13 non-residential) have been damaged due to cloudburst during the interveningnight of August 3-4, 2012 in Uttarkashi, Uttarakhand. There has also been extensivedamage to public utilities in Uttarakhand. No damage has been reported from theGovernment of Himachal Pradesh in this regard, so far.(b)As per the Scheme of financing the assistance for relief expenditure, theState Government concerned is primarily responsible for the execution of the reliefoperations at the ground level in the wake of identified natural calamities which includecloudburst. The Government of India supplements the efforts of the State Governmentsby providing logistic and financial support, where necessary, it is also mentioned thatthe financial assistance to the people affected by such calamities from designated fundof State Disaster Response Fund/National Disaster Response Fund is towards relief &not for compensation of loss. The objective of such fund is to assist the affected personsto start their economic activities again. The relief is by way of gratuitous assistance asan immediate help to overcome the stress.However, Funds to the tune of Rs. 91.46 crore (including Rs. 55.595 crore releasedon 28.06.2012 as 1st instalment of Central share of State Disaster Response Fund forthe year 2011-12) are presently available with the State Government of Uttarakhandfor relief/rescue operations. With regard to Himachal Pradesh 1st instalment of Centralshare of SDRF amounting to Rs. 64.875 crore has been released on 9th August, 2012.

Written Answers to[22 AUGUST, 2012]Unstarred Questions167(b)As per the information furnished by the State Government of Punjab, area-wise and year-wise details of the Sector/projects on which money has been spent inlast five years under BADP are given in the Statement (See below).(c) to (e)It is the primary responsibility of the State Government to undertakeall-round development in the State including border areas. However, to meet the specialdevelopmental needs of the people living in remote and inaccessible areas situatednear the international border and to saturate the border areas with the entire essentialinfrastructure through convergence of Central/State/BADP/Local schemes andparticipatory approach, the Central Government is running a 100% centrally fundedBorder Area Development Programme (BADP).The BADP covers 358 border blocks, which are located along the internationalborder and come under 96 border districts of 17 States viz. Arunachal Pradesh, Assam,Bihar, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram,Nagaland, Punjab, Rajasthan, Sikkim, Tripura, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and WestBengal. Funds are allocated to the States on the basis of (i) length of internationalborder, (ii) population of border blocks, and (iii) area of border blocks with thesecriteria having equal weightage. Besides, 15% weightage is given to hilly, desert andRann of Kutchh areas on account of difficult terrain, scarcity of resources, higher costof construction etc.The policy matters such as the guidelines of BADP , the geographical areas withinwhich the BADP is implemented, allocation of funds, modalities of execution ofschemes etc. is laid down by an Empowered Committee constituted under theChairmanship of the Secretary (Border Management) in the Ministry of Home Affairs.Schemes for each State are approved by the State Level Screening Committee chairedby the Chief Secretary of the State, subject to such general/special directions as givenby the Empowered Committee from time to time.State Governments furnish their Annual Action Plan under BADP every yearduly approved by the SLSC headed by the Chief Secretary of the State.

Shri V .K. Agarwal. The judicial inquiry is in progress.† Original notice of the question was received in Hindi.

178Written Answers to[RAJYA SABHA] Unstarred QuestionsTHE MINISTER OF STA TE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS (SHRIMULLAPPALLY RAMACHANDRAN) : (a)CCTV cameras installed in variousmarkets and border check posts in Delhi are being monitored by Delhi Police on regularbasis.(b) and (c)A project has already been approved by the Government for settingup a comprehensive intelligent CCTV surveillance system for NCT of Delhi.Additionally, Delhi Police have a system of granting licence on the condition that thelicensee shall install CCTV cameras in the premises.(d)CCTV surveillance system helps in detection/prevention of any unlawfulactivity in the area and in monitoring the law & order situation in the area. It also helpsin the identification of criminals/terrorists, if any such person visits the area coveredby CCTV surveillance system. It also helps in detection of crime in the area and alsoacts as a deterrent for criminals and terrorists.Sexual offences against women†1178.DR. PRABHA THAKUR : Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS bepleased to state:(a)the States where there has been an increase in the sexual offences againstwomen and States where it has decreased in comparison to previous period; and(b)the details of reasons observed for such increase and decrease?THE MINISTER OF STA TE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS (SHRIJITENDRA SINGH) : (a) and (b)As per the information provided by the NationalCrime Records Bureau (NCRB) 15 States/UTs had reported increase in sexual offencesconsisting of rape, molestation and sexual harassment during 2011 as compared to2010, whereas, 18 States/UTs had reported decrease during the same period. 2 States/UTs reported no variation. The State/UT-wise details for the years 2009, 2010 and2011 respectively are given in the Statement (See below).The data collected from the States/UTs is based on the crime reported at thePolice Stations. The trends based are purely dependent on the reporting of crime bycitizens and this could be influenced by a number of socio-economic environmentalreasons and hence it is not possible to ascribe any specific reasons for the changingtrends in crime.† Original notice of the question was received in Hindi.

BANDYOPADHY AY : Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRSbe pleased to state:(a)whether Government is aware of the fact that one member of the presentUnion Council of Ministers openly declared that the Sarkeguda police firing on 28thJune, 2012 in Chhattisgarh was a mistake by CRPF;(b)whether a team of 16 members from the coordination of the DemocraticRights Organisation which visited Sarkeguda and other neighbouring villages andinteracted with the local population found the CRPF firing injustified; and(c)if so, what action Government proposes to take to establish the facts,compensate the victims of firing and to prevent recurrence of similar incidents infuture?THE MINISTER OF STA TE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS (SHRIJITENDRA SINGH) : (a)The Ministry of Home Affairs has not received any formalcommunication from any Minister that the Sarkeguda incident of 28th June, 2012 wasa mistake by the CRPF. Shri V .K. Agarwal. The judicial inquiry is in progress.(b)Y es, Sir. The said group from various organizations had visited Sarkegudaon July 6-7, 2012. However, National Human RightsCommission (NHRC), had registered total of 14239 cases of deaths in judicial andpolice custody all over India during the period 2001 to 2010.(b)The reasons for these deaths include natural causes, torture in custody,injuries due to beating by public before arrest, suicide in custody as well as negligenceby the public servants. As per the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India, “Police”and “Public Order” are State Subjects. It is for the State Governments to take action inevery crime. The Central Government issues advisories, while the NHRC issuesguidelines and recommendations in respect of custodial deaths. NHRC has framedguidelines for reporting all deaths in custody whether natural or otherwise, within 24hours of its occurrence. The NHRC also calls for various reports for ascertaining anyfoul play or negligence by public servants, which resulted in custodial death. Written Answers to[22 AUGUST, 2012]Unstarred Questions197THE MINISTER OF HOUSING AND URBAN POVERTY ALLEVIA TION(KUMARI SELJA) : (a) and (b)The Ministry of Housing and Urban PovertyAlleviation is implementing the following schemes for slum dwellers and urban pooracross the country:(i)Under the Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM)launched on 3rd December, 2005, the Basic Services to the Urban Poor(BSUP) and Integrated Housing and Slum Development Programmes(IHSDP) are being implemented which focus on basic services to the urbanpoor and integrated development of slums. Under BSUP , 65 select citiesin the country are covered and the remaining cities are covered underIHSDP . Under BSUP scheme, 527 projects have been approved with totalproject cost of Rs. 30188.69 crores for construction of 1017252 DwellingUnits (DUs). Under IHSDP scheme, 1084 projects in 928 cities have beenapproved with total project cost of Rs. 12048.50 crores for construction of570951 Dwelling Units (DUs).(ii)Swarna Jayanti Shahari Rozgar Y ojana (SJSRY) aims at providing gainfulemployment to the urban unemployed and under-employed poor, throughencouraging the setting up of self-employment ventures by the urban poorliving below the poverty line, skills training and also through providingwage employment by utilizing their labour for construction of sociallyand economically useful public assets. This scheme is applicable to allcities and towns in the country. During the 2011-12, 353,803 beneficiarieswere covered under skills training and 79,804 beneficiaries under urbanself-employment programme components of SJSRY .(iii)In pursuance of the Government’s vision of creating a Slum-free India, anew scheme ‘Rajiv Awas Y ojana’ (RA Y) has been launched on 02.06.2011.Under the Scheme financial assistance is being provided to States that arewilling to assign property rights to slum dwellers for provision of decentshelter and basic civic and social services for slum redevelopment, andfor creation of affordable housing stock. The scheme is expected to coverabove 250 cities, across the entire country by the end of 12th Plan (2017).The States would be required to include all the mission cities of JNNURM,preferably cities with more than 3 lakh population as per 2001 Census;and other smaller cities, with due consideration to the pace of growth of

292Written Answers to[RAJYA SABHA] Unstarred QuestionsProgress of slum rehabilitation project1239.SHRI SALIM ANSARI :SHRI JAI PRAKASH NARAY AN SINGH :Will the Minister of URBAN DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:(a)whether it is a fact that Delhi Development Authority (DDA) had auctioned11.8 acres of land in 2006 in Tehkhand, South Delhi for an on-site slum rehabilitationproject;(b)if so, the progress made so far of the above project; and(c)whether slum dwellers have since been rehabilitated and if not, the reasonstherefor?THE MINISTER OF STA TE IN THE MINISTRY OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT(SHRI SAUGATA RAY) : (a)Yes Sir, DDA has allotted by way of Auction landmeasuring 14.3 hect. at Tehkhand to rehabilitate the Jhuggi Dwellers of the area throughprivate participation. As per scheme, 3500 EWS Houses for Slum Dwellers and 750Houses for free sale by Developers were to be constructed. The possession of 11.70Hect. land (excluding the JJ Cluster measuring 2.6 Hect.) was handed over to thedeveloper on 04.12.2006(b) and (c)The Construction of the project could not be started by the Developerdue to non-receipt of NOC from the Forest and Environmental Department/PollutionControl Board. At present the matter is sub-judice before the Hon’ble Supreme Courtof India.Class-C cities under JNNURM1240.SHRI MANSUKH L. Thirty (30) cities/UAs having population less than onemillion are covered under Category-C of UIG of JNNURM. The city of Porbandar ofGujarat State is included in the Category-C of UIG of JNNURM.(c) and (d)Yes, Sir. As per guidelines of UIG, the number of cities under theMission shall remain around 60.
